prompt_text: How to migrate from Excel to a nonprofit CRM
response_text:
Migrating from Excel to a nonprofit CRM is mostly a **data-cleanup and mapping project**: inventory your spreadsheets, standardize and deduplicate the data, match Excel columns to CRM fields, then import in the right order and verify the results.[1][2]

A practical migration process looks like this:

- **Inventory every data source** first, including every workbook, tab, and any other system that holds donor, volunteer, program, event, or fundraising data.[1][4]
- **Export full datasets** rather than filtered reports, and keep each data type in its own file with the original column headers preserved so you can trace problems later.[1][2]
- **Clean the data in Excel before import** by removing duplicates, standardizing names and formats, and making sure each person or organization has a unique record.[1][2]
- **Map your columns to CRM fields** using the new system’s import template or field structure; nonprofit CRM templates are designed to make this mapping easier.[1][3]
- **Separate data by type** so contacts, donations, recurring gifts, notes, tags, and custom fields are handled as distinct imports when required.[1][2]
- **Import in the correct order**, usually contacts first, then gift history, then recurring gifts, then tags/custom fields, so linked records have something to attach to.[2]
- **Back up everything** in at least two places before importing, and keep the old spreadsheet or system active until you confirm the migration is accurate.[2]
- **Spot-check records after import** by comparing a small sample against the source Excel files to confirm names, gift amounts, dates, and contact details match.[2]

A few nonprofit-specific tips matter:

- If your Excel file contains mixed data types in one sheet, split them before import; most CRMs work best with one dataset per file.[1]
- If some columns do not fit the new CRM, decide whether to create custom fields, convert the data into notes, or archive it separately.[1][5]
- Train a small group of power users first, then expand to the rest of the team after the core workflows are working.[2]
- Set up basics like donation acknowledgments, thank-you emails, and recurring automations before launch so the CRM is usable on day one.[2]
